summary: Vanuatu’s restoration pledge is to restore 25,000 hectares of degraded natural forest and 1,000 hectares of mangrove forest by 2035—about 2.2% of the broader 11,478 km² Forest class. The mixed forest/AFOLU package includes 1,500 hectares of new forest, 1,500 hectares improved with native species, and a 587.07 kt CO₂ eq overall AFOLU emissions reduction through 2035. Conservation targets include six Water Protection Zones, 20 Community Conservation Areas, 40 integrated coastal-management plans, 100 FADs, 100% mapping of forest areas of significance, and at least 17% of important biodiversity areas, 30% of natural forest, 10% of wetlands, 10% of marine areas, plus 30% of the ocean. Agriculture covers all six provinces, targets 30% producer training and 40% pasture conversion, and sets farmer targets of 60–1,000 by 2035; agriculture is 3.7% of land, while grassland extent is not supplied.
